newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shippers expect KLM to drop surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shippers expect KLM to drop surcharge.

text.p: The Dutch shippers organisation (EVO) said it expects KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV to drop its cargo fuel surcharge on April 15.

Hans Leijgraaff, airfreight secretary for the EVO, said he had received a telephone call from KLM's head of Benelux and UK cargo sales saying if fuel prices remain stable the airline would withdraw the fuel surcharge on April 15.
This followed an earlier letter from KLM to the shippers' organisation --representing companies moving goods by air -- stating that it was studying the jet fuel price situation.
The carrier introduced a worldwide cargo fuel surcharge of 0.20 guilders a kg last November 1 following a sharp rise in fuel price and similar moves by other major airlines.
A KLM Cargo spokesman said the airline had sent the letter and made the telephone call, but he declined to definitely confirm the withdrawal of the charge on the 15th.
"It is not a certainty," he said.
Leijgraaff said: "Kerosene prices have dropped to below last July's levels so there is no reason for KLM not to drop the charge."
Last week the Brussels-based European Air Shippers Council(EASC) called for the withdrawal of the surcharge.
So far Delta Airlines, United Airlines and Virgin Atlantic Cargo have all dropped the surcharge.
